Otu made the call while addressing delegates of the 6th African Sub-Sovereign Governments Network Investment Conference (AfSNET 2026) in Calabar. The governor stressed that Cross River is humbled and privileged to host the continental gathering, and expressed happiness at the array of personalities and professionals in attendance. “We are very humbled and privileged to be your hosts for these two days,” he said. “I am so happy to see the array of personalities, professionals that are here with me.” He gave the assurance that Cross River remains the home of hospitality and that delegates would find whatever they came to see in the state. “I want to give you a reassuring guarantee that Cross River State remains the home of hospitality,” he said. “Whatever you want to see, you are going to find.” Otu said improved water infrastructure is critical to raising the level of trade in Africa, which he described as very low. “We are also believing that with the support of African banks, we will have started the process of bringing real water infrastructure developments to this region, so that we are going to have sponsored water,” he said. He said better infrastructure would help regional and small-scale enterprises and businesses to trade across borders, noting that many traders struggle because of poor infrastructure and border challenges. “I am also hoping that this will help us to bring more regional and small scale enterprises and businesses to trade across our borders,” he said. The governor also invited delegates to experience the state’s tourism attractions, including the Obudu Cattle Ranch. “For those who want to touch the clouds, we will take you to the Obudu Cattle Ranch where you can commune with the clouds,” he said, as he once more welcomed all delegates and thanked them for coming.
